title: Three-tier priority burndown — exec scratchpad
content:
Purpose: lightweight rolling list to keep the week focused. I use a three-tier model so I don’t get pulled into busywork. Quick scan every morning, adjust timeblocks, update owners.

Tier 1 — Strategic (must move this week)
- Finalize Dedicated SLA language for sales decks (legal review needed). ETA: Fri COB. Progress: 60% (draft done, legal comments pending).
  - Follow-up: Ruth to push legal on cryptic SOC2 clause — pinged slack #legal, awaiting reply.
  - Outcome needed: updated clause + sample customer contract snippet for AE.
- Private deploy pilot sign-off with BetaCustomerX (security checklist + infra runbook). Meeting Thurs 10:00. Prep: one-pager of rollback plan + test vector list.
  - Action: I will draft rollback bullets today (30m). Maya to own runbook checklist items.
- Approve Dedicated capacity pricing tiers (numbers from finance). Hot decision: keep burst add-on or fold into base?
  - Metric to watch: projected unit cost delta at 75% utilization. Finance note attached.

Tier 2 — Operational (important, not blockers)
- Observability retention policy proposal: recommend 90d default + paid 365d option. Get product sign-off by next Tue.
  - Quick ask: ask observability lead to model cost impact by Friday.
- Model fallback policy doc — need one-liner for onboarding guide. Draft below: "Route fallback to lowest-cost compatible variant; log reason + token delta."
- Optimize experiment: KV cache hit improvement A/B running. Check interim metrics Mon/Wed/Fri.

Tier 3 — Housekeeping / tactical
- Calendar clean-up: block two 60m heads-down slots tomorrow (09:30, 15:30).
- Inbox triage: reply to partner infra request (short yes/no + ask for s3/access).
- People ops: confirm interview panel for infra hire (send confirmation invites).

Today (Fri) timeboxing
- 08:30–09:00: quick triage + patch PR review (runtime/pull/888) — approve or comment.
- 09:00–09:30: SLA deck edits (focus on language clarity).
- 10:00–11:00: BetaCustomerX prep w/ Maya + Eng ops (runbook ownership).
- 11:30–12:00: 1:1 with head of product — agenda: retention policy, pricing tradeoffs.
- 13:00–14:00: Blocked for deep work: draft rollback plan + legal note.
- 15:30–16:00: send interview confirmations + quick hiring scorecard review.

Meeting prep notes (callouts to use in sync)
- SRE sync: ask about degraded fallback latency — is our routing policy causing retries? Bring recent trace examples (link in artifacts).
- Product: present two pricing options + fiscal impact slide; show customer story that prefers simplicity.
- Legal: ask for 3 specific edit suggestions on SLA clause; push for redlines by EOD Thurs.

Action items (owner — eta)
- Ruth Wang — get legal redlines for SLA clause — 2026-03-12 EOD (pending).
- Maya Lopez — complete runbook checklist draft and share — 2026-03-12 17:00 (in progress).
- Finance (Vik) — cost delta spreadsheet for burst add-on vs integrated pricing — 2026-03-14 (requested).
- Eng (Julian) — KV cache A/B metric snapshot for Fri morning — 2026-03-13 (todo).

Quick drafts / copy snippets (paste-ready)
- Customer-facing: "We offer predictable Dedicated capacity with optional burst pools for short-term spikes; our SLA ensures 99.9% availability with automated fallback to compatible model variants to maintain service."
- Internal one-liner: "Default routing favors latency SLOs; cost-oriented customers may opt into cost-first routes."

Unresolved questions / risks
- If legal pushes longer warranty language, could delay customer contracts by 2 weeks — how flexible on interim commitments?
- Burst capacity cost could make quote >25% more expensive for some mid-market customers. Need a tiered approach?
- Observability retention cost balloon if several customers ask for 365d — how to monetize?

Notes to self (shortcuts)
- When pressed in meetings: lead with impact (latency/cost) + proposed decision. Avoid long technical dives unless asked.
- Use the one-pager template for pilots — reduces back-and-forth.
- Keep updates to the exec thread concise: 3 bullets: decision needed, impact, ask.

End-of-day quick burndown (to update before sign-off)
- SLA language: 60% -> target 100% after legal redlines.
- Runbook: 40% -> owner assigned, expect draft by EOD.
- Pricing: analysis requested -> hold decision until finance input.

References / quick links
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/888
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4021 (Private deploy pilot)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ENG-7521 (SLA draft)

End — check this doc before standalone 1:1s and before the BetaCustomerX sync. Keep short, update owners, mark done inline.
